title: How do we find the area of a quadrilateral?
description: A quadrilateral has a diagonal of ten centimetres, and the heights from the two opposite corners to it are four and three centimetres. The diagonal splits the shape into two triangles, and their areas add up to thirty five square centimetres. Keeko doubts the answer of seventy.
teaching_notes: One idea: a diagonal splits a quadrilateral into two triangles, so its area is the sum of two triangle areas. Watch for students who forget the half and say ten times four plus ten times three.

source: A quadrilateral ABCD has diagonal BD = 10 cm. The heights fr
video_script.why: The child sees that a four sided shape with no special sides has no formula of its own, but a diagonal splits it into two triangles whose areas can be added.
video_script.substitution: the book's quadrilateral ABCD with the diagonal BD; BD = 10 cm and the heights from A and C to BD are 4 cm and 3 cm
video_script.anchor: the book's quadrilateral ABCD with the diagonal BD = 10 cm and the dashed heights from A and C to BD
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko multiplies the diagonal by each height and gets seventy square centimetres. He forgot that each triangle is only half of base times height.
video_script.payoff_line: The area is thirty five square centimetres
maths_rules: quadrilateral ABCD with diagonal BD = 10 cm; height from A to BD = 4 cm; height from C to BD = 3 cm
the slip: 10 × 4 + 10 × 3 = 70 forgets the halves; each triangle is half of the rectangle 10 × 4 or 10 × 3
video_script.design: One quadrilateral all video. A diagonal makes two triangles and their areas are added. Keeko's doubt: drop the halves.

<bookmark mark='calc'/>Half of ten times four is twenty square centimetres.

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step two, take the triangle B C D. It has the same base B D, and its height is three.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Half of ten times three is fifteen square centimetres.

marks.join: the two triangles slide together to make the quadrilateral

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step three, the two triangles together make the whole quadrilateral.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Add twenty and fifteen to get thirty five.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, check it another way.
Both triangles share the base B D, so add the heights, four plus three, which is seven.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Half of ten times seven is thirty five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The area is thirty five square centimetres.
